:::{#exr-epe-three-sources}
#### Expected squared prediction error from three sources

Let:

- $\paren{\newpredvar, \newoutvar}$ be a [new observation](#def-new-observation) relative to the random [training set](#def-training-set) $\trainset$, and
- $\predvalf{\predvar}$ be a [prediction](prediction.qmd#def-prediction) at the [covariate](#def-covariate) value $\predvar$.

Assume:

- $\newpredvar = \predvar$,
- the squared [bias](#def-prediction-bias) of $\predvalf{\predvar}$ is $\sqf{\bias{\predvalf{\predvar}}} = 1$,
- the [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance) of $\predvalf{\predvar}$ is $\Var{\predvalf{\predvar}} = 2$, and
- the [population variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance) of the [noise](#def-noise) of $\newoutvar$, the population noise variance $\varpar$, is $\varpar = 3$.

1. What is the [expected squared prediction error](#def-epe) $\epe{\fitproc}{\nobs}{\predvar}$?
2. If we could remove all bias and all variance of $\predvalf{\predvar}$,
   what would the expected squared prediction error at $\predvar$ be?
3. Which of the three quantities
   (the squared bias, the variance of $\predvalf{\predvar}$, and the population noise variance $\varpar$)
   can a better prediction method reduce,
   and which cannot?

:::
